plan: - MCU: ESP32-C3 for processing and Wi-Fi communication.- Actuators: Multiple micro servo motors for joint articulation.- Sensors: IMU (e.g., MPU6050) for balance and orientation.- Power: Small 3.7V LiPo battery with charging module.- Frame: Lightweight 3D-printed humanoid chassis and joint components.- Enclosures: Custom 3D-printed housings for electronics and battery.

subSteps.title: 3D print all structural and mounting components
Clean and deburr all 3D printed parts
Install M2 heat set inserts into all designated mounting points on printed parts
Solder power leads to LiPo Battery and Charging Module
Solder power input/output and signal wires to Voltage Regulator
Solder power and I2C lines to Main Robot Controller and Orientation IMU
Solder power, I2C, and OE control lines to Servo Driver PWM Controller
Prepare and label individual servo power and PWM signal wires for all servos
Connect all servo power and PWM signals to the Servo Driver PWM Controller outputs
Perform continuity checks on all soldered connections and verify power buses with multimeter
Flash initial firmware to the Main Robot Controller (main_mcu)
Connect power and verify 3.3V and 5V rails using multimeter
Verify I2C communication with Orientation IMU and Servo Driver from main_mcu
Test individual servos by sending simple PWM commands through the servo_driver
Calibrate the Orientation IMU sensor
Mount the Main Robot Controller, Charging Module, Voltage Regulator, and Battery to their respective mounts in the Robot Torso Chassis
Mount the Servo Driver PWM Controller into its mount in the Robot Torso Chassis
Assemble the robot head by mounting the IMU and Head Tilt Servo, then connect to Head Pan Servo
Assemble the torso and pelvis, mounting the Torso Yaw Servo and attaching the Head Assembly
Assemble the robot arms: mount servos, attach segments using micro servo horns and screws
Assemble the robot legs: mount servos, attach segments and feet using micro servo horns and screws
Route and secure all electrical wiring within the robot for strain relief and neatness
Perform final system test and calibrate joint limits for all servos

projectDescription: A miniature humanoid robot, controlled by an ESP32-C3, features a realistic, compact form. Multiple micro servo motors enable detailed articulation across its 20+ joints, with an IMU providing orientation feedback, all powered by an integrated LiPo battery system within a 3D-printed chassis.

USB cable compatible with main_mcu for programming
Basic understanding of I2C communication protocols
